card.name: Linking words before chemical interaction verbs
card.fires_on: Small linking words (can, which, is, that, to, a closing bracket) right after a chemical or biochemical subject, just before a verb of binding, contacting, coordinating or forming. Seen mostly in structural biology and chemistry text.

modes.label: Relative words after a residue or ion
modes.description: 'which', 'that' or 'is' following a named residue, ion or group, before a verb of contact or coordination.
modes.example: Mutational studies have shown that Lys456,<< which>> contacts the sulfate, is important for C

modes.label: Modal 'can' before chemical behavior
modes.description: 'can' after a chemical subject, ahead of verbs like undergo or exist.
modes.example: 1,3-butadiene :<< can>> undergo addition via two different modes

modes.label: Link before 'form' verbs
modes.description: 'to' after 'potential', ahead of altering formation of something.
modes.example: Leptin is a cytokine and may have the potential<< to>> alter the formation of cytochrome P

card.writes: It prepares the model to continue with words about forming, taking part in, or being involved in interactions.
card.plain: It fires on little connecting words just before the text says what a molecule binds, joins or forms.
